```{r}
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.align = "center", dev = "pdf")

# Simulated advertising data (as in STA2005S W3/W4):
# radio spend is correlated with TV spend, but revenue depends on TV only.
set.seed(201)
ad_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  spend_radio = runif(100, 0, 3)
)
ad_tbl$spend_tv <- 1.2 * ad_tbl$spend_radio + runif(100, 0, 3)
ad_tbl$revenue <- 10 + 2 * ad_tbl$spend_tv + rnorm(100, sd = 2)

fit_tv <- lm(revenue ~ spend_tv, data = ad_tbl)
fit_radio <- lm(revenue ~ spend_radio, data = ad_tbl)
fit_both <- lm(revenue ~ spend_tv + spend_radio, data = ad_tbl)

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "<0.001" else paste0("=", fmt(p, 2))
r2 <- function(fit) summary(fit)$r.squared
coef_row <- function(fit, term) summary(fit)$coefficients[term, ]

r_tv <- cor(ad_tbl$spend_tv, ad_tbl$revenue)
r_tv_radio <- cor(ad_tbl$spend_tv, ad_tbl$spend_radio)
b_tv <- coef(fit_tv)

col_point <- "#a6cee3"
col_line <- "#003366"
col_accent <- "#e6550d"
col_simple <- "#fc8d62"
col_multiple <- "#66c2a5"
col_est <- "#7b3294"
col_pred <- "#b8860b"

theme_slide <- function(font_size = 18) {
  cowplot::theme_cowplot(font_size = font_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
    )
}
lab_tv <- "TV spend"
lab_radio <- "Radio spend"
lab_rev <- "Revenue"
```

# Correlation summarises the strength of a relationship

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=55%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.6
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| out-width: "100%"
ggplot(ad_tbl, aes(spend_tv, revenue)) +
  geom_point(col = col_point, size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = min(ad_tbl$spend_tv), y = max(ad_tbl$revenue),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, label = paste0("r = ", fmt(r_tv)), size = 6.5) +
  labs(x = lab_tv, y = lab_rev) +
  theme_slide()
```

:::

:::{.column width=45%}

- Advertising spend and revenue across 100 markets

- Correlation coefficient formula:
$$
r=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}
{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\bar x)^2\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-\bar y)^2}}
$$


:::

::::

# Simple linear regression describes the relationship with a line

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=55%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.6
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| out-width: "100%"
ggplot(ad_tbl, aes(spend_tv, revenue)) +
  geom_point(col = col_point, size = 2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = b_tv[1], slope = b_tv[2], col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(x = lab_tv, y = lab_rev) +
  theme_slide()
```

:::

:::{.column width=45%}

\begin{block}{Model}
\centering
$Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X+e,\qquad e\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$
\end{block}

- $\beta_0$: mean of $Y$ when $X=0$
- $\beta_1$: change in the mean of $Y$ for a one-unit increase in $X$
- Fitted line: $\hat{y} = 10.22 + 1.98 x_{\mathrm{TV}}$

:::

::::

# Multiple linear regression uses several predictors at once

Use **multiple** explanatory variables to model one response:

$$
Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\beta_2X_2+\cdots+\beta_pX_p+e,
\qquad
e\sim N(0,\sigma^2)
$$

*Example*: Revenue against TV **and** radio spend:

$$
Y_{\mathrm{Rev}}=\beta_0+\beta_{\mathrm{TV}}X_{\mathrm{TV}}+\beta_{\mathrm{R}}X_{\mathrm{R}}+e
$$

Why care?

- Isolate effects of individual variables
- Greater predictive ability


```{r}
est_tbl <- rbind(
  data.frame(term = "TV", model = "Simple", t(coef_row(fit_tv, "spend_tv")),
             t(confint(fit_tv)["spend_tv", ]), check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(term = "TV", model = "Multiple", t(coef_row(fit_both, "spend_tv")),
             t(confint(fit_both)["spend_tv", ]), check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(term = "Radio", model = "Simple", t(coef_row(fit_radio, "spend_radio")),
             t(confint(fit_radio)["spend_radio", ]), check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(term = "Radio", model = "Multiple", t(coef_row(fit_both, "spend_radio")),
             t(confint(fit_both)["spend_radio", ]), check.names = FALSE)
)
names(est_tbl) <- c("term", "model", "est", "se", "t", "p", "lwr", "upr")
est_tbl$term <- factor(est_tbl$term, levels = c("Radio", "TV"))
est_tbl$model <- factor(est_tbl$model, levels = c("Multiple", "Simple"))
est_radio_s <- est_tbl[est_tbl$term == "Radio" & est_tbl$model == "Simple", ]
est_radio_m <- est_tbl[est_tbl$term == "Radio" & est_tbl$model == "Multiple", ]
est_tv_s <- est_tbl[est_tbl$term == "TV" & est_tbl$model == "Simple", ]
est_tv_m <- est_tbl[est_tbl$term == "TV" & est_tbl$model == "Multiple", ]
```

```{r}
plot_simple <- function(xvar, xlab, fit) {
  ggplot(ad_tbl, aes(.data[[xvar]], revenue)) +
    geom_point(col = col_point, size = 1.8) +
    geom_abline(intercept = coef(fit)[1], slope = coef(fit)[2],
                col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.65) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = lab_rev) +
    theme_slide(font_size = 17)
}
ci_txt <- function(row) paste0("$", fmt(row$lwr), "$ to $", fmt(row$upr), "$")
```

:::{.column width=50%}

```{r}
plot_simple("spend_tv", lab_tv, fit_tv)
```

:::

:::{.column width=50%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.2

```

:::

::::

\begin{block}{Your turn: what happens when we put both in one model?}
\centering
$Y_{\mathrm{Rev}}=\beta_0+\beta_{\mathrm{TV}}X_{\mathrm{TV}}+\beta_{\mathrm{R}}X_{\mathrm{R}}+e$
\end{block}

\pause

\centering
$\hat\beta_{\mathrm{TV}}=`r fmt(est_tv_m$est)`$ (95% CI: `r ci_txt(est_tv_m)`),
\qquad
$\hat\beta_{\mathrm{R}}=`r fmt(est_radio_m$est)`$ (95% CI: `r ci_txt(est_radio_m)`)

```{r}
#| fig-height: 2.3
#| out-width: "95%"
ggplot(ad_tbl, aes(spend_radio, revenue, size = spend_tv, col = spend_tv)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(intercept = coef(fit_radio)[1], slope = coef(fit_radio)[2],
              col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.8, 5), name = lab_tv) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#c6dbef", high = col_line, name = lab_tv) +

```

:::

::::

\begin{block}{The key change in interpretation}
\small
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Simple}: $\beta_{\mathrm{R}}$ is the change in mean revenue for a one-unit increase in radio spend
\item \emph{Multiple}: $\beta_{\mathrm{R}}$ is the change in mean revenue for a one-unit increase in radio spend, \textbf{holding TV spend fixed}
\end{itemize}
\end{block}


# Is radio related to revenue once TV is accounted for?

```{r}
t_s <- est_radio_s$t
t_m <- est_radio_m$t
df_s <- df.residual(fit_radio)
df_m <- df.residual(fit_both)
t_lim <- max(4, ceiling(abs(t_s)) + 1)
t_grid <- data.frame(t = seq(-t_lim, t_lim, length.out = 400))
t_grid$dens <- dt(t_grid$t, df = df_m)
crit <- qt(0.975, df = df_m)
p_null <- ggplot(t_grid, aes(t, dens)) +
  geom_area(data = subset(t_grid, t <= -crit), fill = "grey75") +
  geom_area(data = subset(t_grid, t >= crit), fill = "grey75") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 0.45)) +
  labs(x = "t statistic for radio", y = expression("Density under " * H[0])) +
  theme_slide(font_size = 17) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
```

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=55%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.8
#| fig-height: 3.3
#| out-width: "100%"
p_null
```

:::

:::{.column width=45%}

- Hypotheses:
$$
H_0:\beta_{\mathrm{R}}=0
\quad\text{vs}\quad
H_1:\beta_{\mathrm{R}}\neq0
$$

- Test statistic:
$$
t=\frac{\hat\beta_{\mathrm{R}}}{SE(\hat\beta_{\mathrm{R}})}
$$

:::

::::

# Radio is significant alone, but not once TV is accounted for

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=55%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.8
#| fig-height: 3.3
#| out-width: "100%"
p_null +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t_s, col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t_m, col = col_multiple, linewidth = 1.1) +
  annotate("text", x = t_s, y = 0.38, label = "Simple", col = col_simple,
           hjust = 1.1, size = 5.5) +
  annotate("text", x = t_m, y = 0.42, label = "Multiple", col = col_multiple,
           hjust = -0.1, size = 5.5)
```

:::

:::{.column width=45%}

- Simple: $t=`r fmt(t_s)`$, $p`r fmt_p(est_radio_s$p)`$
  - Reject $H_0$

- Multiple: $t=`r fmt(t_m)`$, $p`r fmt_p(est_radio_m$p)`$
  - Do not reject $H_0$

- Same test as in first year; the question changes: is radio related to revenue **once TV is accounted for**?

:::


::::

# $R^2$ captures how well our model explains the response

```{r}
y_rev <- ad_tbl$revenue
var_y <- var(y_rev)
y_lim <- range(y_rev)
lab_y <- expression("Revenue (" * Y * ")")
lab_yhat <- expression("Predicted revenue (" * hat(Y) * ")")
fig_dir <- knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path")
save_fig <- function(p, name, width = 4.6, height = 3.7) {
  f <- paste0(fig_dir, name, ".pdf")
  dir.create(dirname(f), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ggsave(f, p, width = width, height = height)
  f
}

# Simulated predictors with a chosen correlation with revenue:
# X1 is only slightly related, X2 more strongly than TV spend
sim_x <- function(r, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  z_rev <- as.numeric(scale(y_rev))
  x <- r * z_rev + sqrt(1 - r^2) * rnorm(length(y_rev))
  3 * (x - min(x)) / diff(range(x))
}
x_weak <- sim_x(0.15, 7)
x_strong <- sim_x(0.87, 7)
fit_weak <- lm(y_rev ~ x_weak)
fit_strong <- lm(y_rev ~ x_strong)
lab_weak <- expression(X[1] * " (simulated)")
lab_strong <- expression(X[2] * " (simulated)")

r2_scatter <- function(x, fit, xlab, show_fit) {
  d <- data.frame(x = x, y = y_rev, yhat = fitted(fit))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y))
  if (show_fit) {
    p <- p + geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = yhat), col = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3)
  }
  p <- p +
    geom_point(col = col_point, size = 1.3) +
    annotate("text", x = min(x), y = max(y_rev), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4.3,
             label = paste0("Var(Y)~'='~'", fmt(var_y), "'"), parse = TRUE) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = expression(Y)) +
    theme_slide(font_size = 13)
  if (show_fit) {
    p <- p + geom_abline(intercept = coef(fit)[1], slope = coef(fit)[2],
                         col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.5)
  }
  p
}

hist_breaks <- seq(floor(y_lim[1]), ceiling(y_lim[2]), by = 1)
r2_hist <- function(fit) {
  ggplot(data.frame(yhat = fitted(fit)), aes(yhat)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = hist_breaks, fill = col_simple, col = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
    annotate("text", x = y_lim[1], y = Inf, hjust = 0, vjust = 1.3, size = 4.3,
             label = paste0("Var(hat(Y))~'='~'", fmt(var(fitted(fit))), "'"), parse = TRUE) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = range(hist_breaks)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.45))) +
    labs(x = expression(hat(Y)), y = "Count") +
    theme_slide(font_size = 13)
}

r2_txt <- function(fit) {
  v_hat <- var(fitted(fit))
  paste0("$R^2=", fmt(v_hat), "/", fmt(var_y), "=", fmt(v_hat / var_y), "$")
}

fig_w <- 3.3
fig_h <- 3.7
f_r2_left_1 <- save_fig(
  cowplot::plot_grid(r2_scatter(x_weak, fit_weak, lab_weak, FALSE),
                     NULL, ncol = 1, align = "v"),
  "r2-left-1", width = fig_w, height = fig_h
)
f_r2_left_2 <- save_fig(
  cowplot::plot_grid(r2_scatter(x_weak, fit_weak, lab_weak, TRUE),
                     r2_hist(fit_weak), ncol = 1, align = "v"),
  "r2-left-2", width = fig_w, height = fig_h
)
f_r2_right <- save_fig(
  cowplot::plot_grid(r2_scatter(x_strong, fit_strong, lab_strong, TRUE),
                     r2_hist(fit_strong), ncol = 1, align = "v"),
  "r2-right", width = fig_w, height = fig_h
)
```

\centering
$R^2=\dfrac{\text{Explained variation}}{\text{Total variation}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{Var}(\hat Y)}{\mathrm{Var}(Y)};\qquad \hat Y=\hat\beta_0+\hat\beta_1X$

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=48%}

\centering
\only<1>{\includegraphics[height=5.2cm]{`r f_r2_left_1`}}\only<2->{\includegraphics[height=5.2cm]{`r f_r2_left_2`}}

\visible<2->{`r r2_txt(fit_weak)`}

:::

:::{.column width=48%}

\centering
\visible<3>{\includegraphics[height=5.2cm]{`r f_r2_right`}}

\visible<3>{`r r2_txt(fit_strong)`}

:::

::::

# $R^2$ is the squared correlation between the response and the fitted values

```{r}
rev_breaks <- seq(8, 24, by = 4)
cor_panel <- function(x, fit, xlab) {
  d <- data.frame(x = x, y = y_rev, yhat = fitted(fit))
  r <- cor(d$y, d$yhat)
  top <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(col = col_point, size = 1.3) +
    geom_abline(intercept = coef(fit)[1], slope = coef(fit)[2],
                col = col_simple, linewidth = 1.5) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = expression(Y)) +
    theme_slide(font_size = 13)
  bottom <- ggplot(d, aes(yhat, y)) +
    geom_point(col = col_point, size = 1.3) +
    annotate("text", x = y_lim[1], y = y_lim[2], hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4.3,
             label = paste0("r~'='~'", fmt(r), "'*','~~r^2~'='~'", fmt(r^2), "'"),
             parse = TRUE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = rev_breaks) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = rev_breaks) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = y_lim, ylim = y_lim) +
    labs(x = expression(hat(Y)), y = expression(Y)) +
    theme_slide(font_size = 13)
  cowplot::plot_grid(top, bottom, ncol = 1, align = "v")
}
```

\centering
$R^2=\mathrm{cor}(Y,\hat Y)^2$

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width=48%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 3.4
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "74%"
cor_panel(x_weak, fit_weak, lab_weak)
```

:::

:::{.column width=48%}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 3.4
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "74%"
cor_panel(x_strong, fit_strong, lab_strong)
```

:::

::::

# Adding TV to radio doubles $R^2$

```{r}
pred_tbl <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = "Radio only", observed = ad_tbl$revenue, predicted = fitted(fit_radio)),
  data.frame(model = "TV and radio", observed = ad_tbl$revenue, predicted = fitted(fit_both))
)
pred_tbl$model <- factor(pred_tbl$model, levels = c("Radio only", "TV and radio"))
r2_labs <- c(
  "Radio only" = paste0("Radio only\nR\u00b2 = ", fmt(r2(fit_radio))),
  "TV and radio" = paste0("TV and radio\nR\u00b2 = ", fmt(r2(fit_both)))
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 3.1
#| out-width: "78%"
ggplot(pred_tbl, aes(predicted, observed, col = model)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, col = "grey40", linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~model, labeller = as_labeller(r2_labs)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_simple, col_multiple)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(12, 16, 20)) +
  labs(x = lab_yhat, y = lab_y) +
  theme_slide(font_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"))
```

- Prediction is the same idea: $\hat y=\hat\beta_0+\hat\beta_{\mathrm{TV}}\text{TV}+\hat\beta_{\mathrm{R}}\text{Radio}$ is our best (unbiased) prediction of the mean
- Adding a useful predictor (TV) raises $R^2$ and pulls predictions closer to observations

# Almost everything carries over from simple to multiple regression

\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.15\linewidth}p{0.37\linewidth}p{0.44\linewidth}@{}}
 & \textbf{Simple} & \textbf{Multiple} \\
\hline
Model & $Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X+e$, \newline $e\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ & $Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\dots+\beta_pX_p+e$, \newline $e\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ \\
Interpretation & $\beta_1$: change in mean $Y$ for a one-unit increase in $X$ & $\beta_j$: change in mean $Y$ for a one-unit increase in $X_j$, \textbf{holding the other predictors fixed} \\
Hypothesis test & $H_0:\beta_1=0$ vs $H_1:\beta_1\neq0$ \newline $t=\hat\beta_1/SE(\hat\beta_1)\sim t_{n-2}$ & $H_0:\beta_j=0$ vs $H_1:\beta_j\neq0$ \newline $t=\hat\beta_j/SE(\hat\beta_j)\sim t_{n-p-1}$ \\
Fitted values & $\hat Y=\hat\beta_0+\hat\beta_1X$ & $\hat Y=\hat\beta_0+\hat\beta_1X_1+\dots+\hat\beta_pX_p$ \\
$R^2$ & $\dfrac{\text{Explained variation}}{\text{Total variation}}=\mathrm{cor}(Y,\hat Y)^2$ & $\dfrac{\text{Explained variation}}{\text{Total variation}}=\mathrm{cor}(Y,\hat Y)^2$ \\
\end{tabular}

# Multiple regression isolates individual effects and predicts better

Multiple linear regression lets us:

- **Isolate the effects of individual variables**
  - Each coefficient describes one variable, holding the others fixed
  - Radio seemed to matter alone, but not once TV was accounted for

- **Strengthen predictive power**
  - More useful predictors $\Rightarrow$ higher $R^2$ and better predictions
